result:
On the last Tuesday of October, Mara found a door behind the library shelves where the atlas of imaginary islands had leaned against the wall. It was narrow, painted the color of weak tea, and its brass handle felt warm, as though someone waiting inside had only just let go. Beyond it lay a staircase descending through smells of dust, rain, and oranges, toward a soft applause that might have been water somewhere far below. Mara should have fetched the head librarian, but instead she tightened her scarf and went down, holding the rail with both hands like a child. At the bottom, an old woman sat mending coats beside a river crowded with small boats, each carrying a single lighted window in its bow.

Without looking up, the woman said that every coat belonged to a winter somebody had survived, and every pocket held its weather folded neatly inside. She offered Mara a gray sleeve, and Mara understood, with sorrow, that she was being asked to remember an unnamed stranger she had never met. Outside, above them, the library would be opening soon; readers would stamp their shoes, unaware of the dark current and patient mending below their feet. Mara threaded a needle, pricked her finger, and watched one bright bead fall, becoming below her a star no map had recorded or ever would. When she finally climbed back, morning had silvered the windows, and the atlas lay shut, though somewhere inside it, rain was falling softly without end.
